label: early-sequence (t=2-4) input after two or more of {h,1,v,m,j,k,b}, esp. <DEL> in short sequences
explanation: Sparse unit (about 1% of steps) that sits almost entirely in steps t=2-5 of the original/delimiter phases: 54% of mass in the original phase, 39% on <DEL> (rate 4.7% at L=3, 2.8% at L=4, falling for longer L). It essentially never fires at t=0 and rarely in the copy phase (7% of mass). Within that window it is driven by token identity: the prefix contains letters/digits from {h,1,v,m,j,k,b}, h above all (prev_tok=h lift 7.7x, first_tok=h 5.2x), and the current input is <DEL> or one of {i,1,m,v,y,h,a,3}. The largest activations are <DEL> right after a short prefix ending in h, e.g. b h <DEL>. Firing on these tokens is far from reliable, since about 60% of matching steps stay inactive, so the selectivity is a soft combination of token identities that this predicate only approximates. Dev results: F1 0.39, mass recall 0.54.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the input two steps back (most: h, 1, v, m, k, j; least: f, t, r, s) and the previous input (most: h, 1, v, m, j, 2; least: d, w, s, t); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=2, t=1.
